name: rs5c313_rtc_set_time
prose: Precondition: tm points to a struct rtc_time whose tm_sec, tm_min, tm_hour, tm_mday, tm_mon + 1, tm_year % 100 and tm_wday values are valid inputs to bin2bcd; dev may be NULL (rs5c313_check_xstp_bit calls this function with NULL) and is used only in the timeout message. Postcondition: it repeatedly (CE enabled, control register written with 0x04, control register read) tests the ADJ_BSY flag; if the flag is clear it leaves the loop. After a failed test it runs RS5C313_MISCOP, disables CE, waits 700 ns, and then, if its attempt counter (post-incremented) was already above 100, logs a timeout with dev_err and returns -EIO without writing any time register; this means up to 102 tests are made, the flag having to be clear on one of them for the function to continue. When the flag is found clear it writes SEC and SEC10, MIN and MIN10, HOUR and HOUR10, DAY and DAY10, MON and MON10, YEAR and YEAR10 and WEEK from tm (month stored as tm_mon + 1, year as tm_year % 100), disables CE, waits 700 ns and returns 0. It acquires no lock.
note: reviewer (round 15: dev may be NULL) right: rtc-rs5c313.c:355 passes NULL; the 102-attempt count (cnt++ > 100 at line 292) was already stated correctly. Function at rtc-rs5c313.c:273-329.

name: rv3032_handle_irq
prose: Precondition: dev_id is the driver's struct rv3032_data with a valid regmap and rtc. Postcondition: it returns IRQ_NONE if the regmap_read of RV3032_STATUS fails or the value read is 0. Otherwise it returns IRQ_HANDLED. If the status has any of the TF, AF or UF bits set it builds an event mask (RTC_PF for TF, RTC_AF for AF, RTC_UF for UF) and an enable-bit mask (TIE, AIE, UIE for the same flags), calls rtc_update_irq with that event mask, then calls regmap_update_bits on RV3032_STATUS with the whole status value that was read as the mask and 0 as the value (so every bit that was read as set is cleared, not only TF, AF and UF), and regmap_update_bits on RV3032_CTRL2 clearing the TIE/AIE/UIE bits that correspond to the flags found; failures of those two updates are ignored. If none of TF, AF, UF is set, nothing is reported or written and it still returns IRQ_HANDLED.
note: reviewer (round 15: it clears all set STATUS bits, not only TF/AF/UF) right: rtc-rv3032.c:216 uses mask = status. Function at 185-221.

name: sun6i_a31_rtc_clk_init
prose: Precondition: node is the device-tree node matched by the compatible string "allwinner,sun6i-a31-rtc" through CLK_OF_DECLARE_DRIVER. Postcondition: it returns nothing and only forwards to sun6i_rtc_clk_init(node, &sun6i_a31_rtc_data), where the data has rc_osc_rate 667000 and has_prescaler 1; everything else is done by the callee.
note: listed name sun6i_rtc_gettime_wrapper_a31 does not exist; the one-line forwarder for the a31 data is sun6i_a31_rtc_clk_init (rtc-sun6i.c:333-336), identified from the 'a31' in the name and the 'delegates with SoC-specific data' description. Not verified which of the sibling wrappers (a23, h3, h6, r40, v3) the original item meant.

name: dasd_eckd_format_process_data
prose: Precondition: base is a dasd_device with ECKD private data, fdata points to format data, fmt_buffer is NULL or has room for rpt records per track processed, irb may be NULL. Postcondition: it first calls dasd_eckd_format_sanity_checks and returns its -EINVAL (start_unit or stop_unit at or beyond real_cyl * trk_per_cyl, start_unit greater than stop_unit, or an invalid blksize) with fdata untouched. Otherwise it saves the old start and stop units, chooses a step (1 for command-mode format check, DASD_CQR_MAX_CCW / rpt for transport-mode check, DASD_CQR_MAX_CCW / recs_per_track otherwise) and loops building CCW requests with dasd_eckd_format_build_ccw_req, queueing them and advancing start_unit. If the builder returns -ENOMEM with an empty queue it returns -ENOMEM; with a non-empty queue it stops building, runs the queued requests and then continues the outer loop with the remaining tracks. Any other builder error skips running the queue (the requests already queued are freed without being run) and is returned unchanged unless it is -EIO. It runs the queue with dasd_sleep_on_queue and then, for every queued request, frees it and decrements the device's count; if a request status is DASD_CQR_FAILED the result becomes -EIO, and when fmt_buffer and irb are both non-NULL the failed request's irb is copied into *irb and the sense pointer is taken from it (that pointer refers into the failed request's data, which the same loop frees). A non-zero result other than -EIO is returned as is; -EIO is turned into a retry of the outer loop only if sense is available and its byte 1 has No Record Found or File Protected, otherwise -EIO is returned. On such a retry the loop builds requests only for tracks not yet queued (start_unit has advanced); when none remain, the empty queue run overwrites the result, normally with 0, but when tracks remain after an earlier -ENOMEM split they are built and run too, so the final result is that of the last pass. After the sanity checks, every return restores fdata->start_unit and stop_unit to their saved values.
note: reviewer (round 15: after a mid-build -ENOMEM the retry can build more requests, so it does not simply return 0) right; round 2 (early -ENOMEM leaves start_unit unchanged) is covered by the restore at out. dasd_eckd.c:3013-3135; slice cut the head.

name: count_exts
prose: Precondition: trks_per_ext > 0 and the values are small enough that the intermediate sums do not overflow. Postcondition: returns 1 if from == to. Otherwise it counts a first partial extent when from is not a multiple of trks_per_ext (cur_pos becomes the number of tracks from from to the end of that extent, capped at to), then, if at least trks_per_ext tracks remain after from + cur_pos, adds the number of whole extents in that remainder and sets cur_pos to the last track of them, and finally adds 1 if cur_pos < to. When from is 0 or a multiple of trks_per_ext the result equals to / trks_per_ext - from / trks_per_ext + 1. When from is not a multiple, cur_pos is an offset after the first step but an absolute track number after the full-extent step, and the last comparison with to mixes the two, so the result can be one larger than the number of extents the range touches (for example from=54, to=102, trks_per_ext=172 gives 2 although the range lies in one extent). It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires from <= to && trks_per_ext > 0 && to <= 2147483647 && (from == to || from % trks_per_ext == 0); ensures result == to / trks_per_ext - from / trks_per_ext + 1; */
note: the prose claimed the exact number of intersecting extents; hand trace of from=54, to=102, trks_per_ext=172 (dasd_eckd.c:3738-3753) gives 2, matching the random-testing counterexample, so the claim is false for unaligned from. The contract is restricted to from == to or from aligned, where the trace matches the formula. Function at dasd_eckd.c:3728-3756.

name: dasd_path_notoper_all
note: no function named dasd_path_notoper_all in dasd_int.h; the nearby inline functions are dasd_path_notoper (1438) and dasd_path_no_path (1453), and the packet gives no prose to decide which was meant.

name: con3215_init
prose: Precondition: none; run once as the console initcall (__init). Postcondition: returns -ENODEV (-19) if CONSOLE_IS_3215 is false. Otherwise, on z/VM it issues two cpcmd commands, then allocates NR_3215_REQ request structures onto raw3215_freelist; if an allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM (-12) and the requests already allocated stay on the freelist. It then creates the console ccw device; if that fails it returns -ENODEV (the freelist is kept). It allocates raw3215_alloc_info (result not checked), sets raw3215[0], and if ccw_device_enable_console fails it destroys the console device, frees the info, clears raw3215[0] and returns -ENODEV; if raw3215_startup fails it frees the info, clears raw3215[0] and returns -ENODEV (without destroying the console device). On success it registers the panic notifier, the reboot notifier and the console and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round 15: contract omits side effects; also mismatched the -ENODEV list) right; contract dropped since the function sets globals. con3215.c:899-953.

name: sclp_check_interface
prose: Precondition: not called with sclp_lock held; the global sclp_init_req and its SCCB are usable. Postcondition: it takes sclp_lock with interrupts saved and calls register_external_irq; if that fails it releases the lock and returns the error. Otherwise it makes up to SCLP_INIT_RETRY + 1 attempts (an attempt counter reset can add more, see below): each builds an init request and calls sclp_service_call_trace; if that returns -EIO the loop ends with -EIO; otherwise it marks the request running, arms a retry timer, drops the lock, enables the service-signal interrupt subclass, waits, disables it, retakes the lock, deletes the timer and sets rc = -EBUSY; if sclp_init_req.status is SCLP_REQ_DONE and the response code is 0x20 it sets rc = 0 and stops, and if the status is SCLP_REQ_DONE and the response code is 0x74f0 it sets sclp_mask_compat_mode to true (when not already set) and resets the counter so the loop runs again. If the loop ends without success rc is -EBUSY (or -EIO from the service call). After the loop, when registration had succeeded, it unregisters the external irq handler and releases the lock on all exits, and returns rc.
note: reviewer (round 15: success needs sclp_init_req.status == SCLP_REQ_DONE as well as response code 0x20) right, sclp.c:1178-1181; the -EIO return (round 0) is covered. Slice cut the head; function at sclp.c:1141-1193.

name: __tape_do_irq
prose: Precondition: called as the ccw interrupt handler; intparm is the tape_request pointer (possibly NULL) and irb is a valid irb or an error pointer; if the irb shows a deferred start error (cc non-zero with the start-function bit) the request must be non-NULL, because its status is read. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once if dev_get_drvdata gives no tape device. If irb is an error pointer: -ETIMEDOUT (logged) and -EIO end the request with -EIO via __tape_end_request, any other error is only logged, and it returns. If cc is non-zero, the start-function bit is set and the request is in TAPE_REQUEST_IN_IO, it sets the request to TAPE_REQUEST_QUEUED, schedules tape_dnr one second later and returns. Otherwise it stores the irb residual count in request->rescnt when request is non-NULL; with a NULL request and device status 0x85 or 0x80 and a non-empty request queue whose first request is TAPE_REQUEST_LONG_BUSY, it deletes the long-busy timer, and only if the timer was pending drops a device reference and starts the next request, and then returns in all such cases (it does not continue when the timer was not pending). Then it sets GMT_ONLINE from sense byte 1 for a device status other than 0x0c and dumps sense, or sets GMT_ONLINE for 0x0c; returns if tape_state is TS_NOT_OPER (after rescnt was stored); ends a TAPE_REQUEST_DONE request with -EIO and returns; otherwise calls device->discipline->irq and acts on its result: TAPE_IO_SUCCESS ends the request with that code (setting GMT_ONLINE), TAPE_IO_PENDING does nothing, TAPE_IO_LONG_BUSY sets the long-busy timer and the request status, TAPE_IO_RETRY restarts via __tape_start_io (ending the request with the error if that fails), TAPE_IO_STOP cancels via __tape_cancel_io (ending with the error if that fails), and any other code ends the request with -EIO if positive and with the code itself if negative.
note: reviewer (round 15: after the long-busy timer check the function returns unconditionally, it does not fall through) right, tape_core.c:1110-1117; round 2 (TS_NOT_OPER return happens after rescnt is set) is consistent with the new text. Function at tape_core.c:1052-1192.

name: airq_init
prose: Precondition: none (called once at init). Postcondition: it creates the DMA pool "airq_iv_cache" with dma_pool_create on the css DMA device, using cache_line_size() as size and alignment and PAGE_SIZE as boundary, stores the result in the global airq_iv_cache, and returns -ENOMEM if the result is NULL and 0 otherwise. It takes no lock; the pool stays in the global.
note: airq.c:305-313. Contract dropped because the function writes a global and calls helpers.

name: ccw_request_start
prose: Precondition: cdev's private->req has its lpm, maxretries, singlepath, cp, timeout, callback and data fields set. Postcondition: it sets req->mask to 0x8080 when req->singlepath is set and to req->lpm otherwise, sets req->retries to req->maxretries, replaces req->mask with lpm_adjust(req->mask, req->lpm), and sets req->drc, req->done and req->cancel to 0. If the mask is then 0 it calls ccwreq_stop(cdev, -EACCES), which sets done, disarms the timeout (ccw_device_set_timeout 0), clears the irb and calls req->callback(cdev, req->data, -EACCES) once. Otherwise it calls ccwreq_do, which loops over the mask: it consumes a retry or moves to the next path (clearing the mask when not singlepath); for each attempt it clears the irb and calls cio_start; on success it calls ccw_device_set_timeout(req->timeout) and returns with the request pending and no callback; on -ENODEV it calls ccwreq_stop with -ENODEV; on -EACCES it moves to the next path; on any other error it calls cio_clear: if that succeeds it returns with the request pending without calling ccw_device_set_timeout and without invoking the callback, and if cio_clear fails it calls ccwreq_stop with that error. When the mask runs out ccwreq_stop is called with -EACCES. Each ccwreq_stop invokes the callback once with the code (req->drc is 0 here, so the code is not replaced).
note: reviewer (round 15: the 'timeout not armed' claim after a successful cio_clear is unsupported; the code neither arms nor disarms it on that path) right; the sentence now says only that ccw_device_set_timeout is not called. ccwreq.c:120-142, ccwreq_do 75-112, ccwreq_stop 58-70.

name: chsc_async
prose: Precondition: interrupts are disabled and chsc_lock is held (stated in the function's comment), chsc_area and request are valid. Postcondition: it sets chsc_area->header.key, then loops over chsc subchannels returned by chsc_get_next_subchannel (each returned with a device reference). For a subchannel under sch->lock: if private->request is already set it unlocks, records -EBUSY and moves on without setting header.sid and without calling put_device (the reference taken for that subchannel is not dropped by this function); otherwise it sets chsc_area->header.sid and issues the chsc instruction: cc 0 gives 0, cc 1 sets the start-function bit in the subchannel's schib, stores request in private->request and gives -EINPROGRESS, cc 2 gives -EBUSY, any other cc gives -ENODEV. After unlocking, -EINPROGRESS is returned at once with the device reference kept; for the other outcomes it calls put_device and, if the result was 0, returns 0. When the loop ends it returns the result of the last subchannel examined (-EBUSY or -ENODEV), or -ENODEV if no subchannel was found. No request is registered on a subchannel unless -EINPROGRESS is returned.
note: reviewer (round 15: header.sid is not set for busy subchannels that are skipped) right, chsc_sch.c:216-221. Function at chsc_sch.c:203-252.

name: cio_dma_pool_init
prose: Precondition: none beyond the css DMA device returned by cio_get_dma_css_dev() existing. Postcondition: it stores the result of cio_gp_dma_create(cio_get_dma_css_dev(), 1) in the global cio_dma_pool and returns -ENOMEM if that result is NULL (gen_pool_create failed) and 0 otherwise. A non-NULL pool may hold no memory if dma_alloc_coherent failed inside cio_gp_dma_create, which returns the pool anyway. The pool is never released by this function.
note: reviewer (round 15: contract omits the cio_dma_pool assignment) right; contract dropped because the function writes a global. css.c:1079-1086, cio_gp_dma_create 1039-1058.

name: ccw_purge_blacklisted
prose: Precondition: process context; for_each_subchannel_staged and purge_fn can be used. Postcondition: it logs an event message, calls for_each_subchannel_staged(purge_fn, NULL, NULL) and ignores that call's result, and returns 0 on its only return statement. purge_fn may return -EINTR when a signal is pending, which can end the iteration early, but that value is not returned by this function.

name: zcrypt_rsa_crt
prose: Precondition: perms and crt are valid, tr may be NULL, and the caller does not hold zcrypt_list_lock. Postcondition: returns a long: it calls ap_init_apmsg and goes to the exit with its error if it fails; returns -EINVAL if crt->outputdatalength < crt->inputdatalength; otherwise sets crt->outputdatalength = crt->inputdatalength (left in place if a later step fails), calls get_rsa_crt_fc and goes to the exit with its error if it fails; then, holding zcrypt_list_lock, picks the best card and queue (online, usable, permitted, within modulus-size limits, with a retry penalty when tr says the same card or queue was just used) and calls zcrypt_pick_queue; if no queue is picked it returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it calls the queue's rsa_modexpo_crt op, takes zcrypt_list_lock again and calls zcrypt_drop_queue, and returns the op's result. At the common exit it always calls ap_release_apmsg and, if tr is non-NULL, sets tr->last_rc to the returned value and tr->last_qid to the queue id used (0 when no queue was picked).
note: listed name _zcrypt_send_crt does not exist; the function in the slice is zcrypt_rsa_crt (zcrypt_api.c:747-850), slice cut the head. At the exit ap_release_apmsg is also reached when ap_init_apmsg fails.

name: chx_txdone
prose: Precondition: arg is the struct channel whose transmit CCW completed, with transmitted skbs on ch->io_queue and possibly data on ch->collect_queue; the caller does not hold ch->collect_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It updates the profile times, logs if the CCW count is non-zero, deletes the channel timer, and for every skb dequeued from io_queue adds one packet and skb->len - LL_HEADER_LENGTH bytes (plus 2 for the first) to the stats, drops its user count and frees it with dev_kfree_skb_irq. Then, under ch->collect_lock, it clears the normalized CDA of ccw[4]. If ch->collect_len > 0 and ctcm_checkalloc_buffer(ch) returns non-zero it unlocks and returns at once, leaving the state unchanged and without calling ctcm_clear_busy_do. If collect_len > 0 and the buffer is fine, it packs the collect_queue skbs into trans_skb behind a 2-byte length, counts and frees them, clears collect_len, unlocks, arms the 5 second timer, starts a chained transmit with ccw_device_start, and if that fails it adds the packet count to tx_dropped and tx_errors, deletes the timer and calls ctcm_ccw_check_rc. If collect_len is 0 it unlocks and sets the channel state to CTC_STATE_TXIDLE. In both of these cases it then calls ctcm_clear_busy_do(dev).
note: listed name ctcm_chx_tx does not exist; the prose describes chx_txdone (ctcm_fsms.c:246-323), which lies in the slice. Previously dropped.

name: mpc_send_qllc_discontact
prose: Precondition: dev is a net_device whose ml_priv is a ctcm_priv with a valid mpcg group. Postcondition: it switches on grp->saved_state. For the XID states (XID0IOWAIT, XID0IOWAIX, XID7INITI, XID7INITZ, XID2INITW, XID2INITX, XID7INITW, XID7INITX) with grp->estconnfunc non-NULL it calls estconnfunc(grp->port_num, -1, 0), sets estconnfunc to NULL and returns 0. For an XID state with no estconnfunc, and for MPCG_STATE_FLOWC and MPCG_STATE_READY, it sets grp->send_qllc_disc to 2 and allocates an skb with GFP_ATOMIC: if the allocation fails it logs, increments priv->stats.rx_dropped and returns -ENOMEM; otherwise it fills a qllc header (address 0xcc, command 0x03), and if the headroom is below 4 it logs, frees the skb (rx_dropped is not incremented) and returns -ENOMEM; otherwise it pushes the read channel's pdu_seq as 4 bytes, increments that pdu_seq and then sets it to 0, sets the skb fields and passes it to netif_rx, and returns 0. For any other state it does nothing and returns 0.
note: real name mpc_send_qllc_discontact (ctcm_mpc.c:2047-2125); listed 'unnamed' item. The old prose called the argument grp and said rx_dropped is incremented on the headroom failure, which the code does not do.

name: qeth_core_init
prose: Precondition: none; run once at module load (__init). Postcondition: it logs, creates the debugfs directory "qeth" (the result is not checked) and then, in order, registers the DBF views, registers the root device "qeth", creates the qeth_hdr, qeth_buf and qeth_qaob slab caches, registers the qeth ccw driver and then the ccwgroup driver, returning 0 if all succeed. On a failure it returns the negative errno of the failing step (-ENOMEM for a cache, the PTR_ERR of the root device, or the registration error) after logging 'Initializing the qeth device driver failed' and undoing the earlier steps: if the ccwgroup registration fails it unregisters the ccw driver (the ccwgroup driver was never registered, so no path unregisters it); then it destroys the qaob, outbuf and header caches that were created, unregisters the root device (only if it was registered), unregisters the DBF views (only if registered), and always calls debugfs_remove_recursive on the debugfs directory.
note: reviewer (round 15: the failure path never unregisters the CCW-group driver, only the CCW driver) right, qeth_core_main.c:7147-7157; the old text listed both. Function at 7108-7172.

name: ZFCP_SHOST_ATTR(_name, _format, _arg...)
prose: Macro-generated function: ZFCP_SHOST_ATTR(_name, _format, _arg...) defines a sysfs show function zfcp_sysfs_adapter_<_name>_show(dev, attr, buf) and a read-only device attribute for it. The generated function calls zfcp_sysfs_adapter_ex_config(dev, &stat_info); if that returns non-zero (-EOPNOTSUPP when the adapter lacks the measurement-data feature, -ENOMEM, or the result of the exchange-config call, including -EAGAIN) it returns that value and writes nothing to buf; otherwise it returns the length written by sysfs_emit(buf, _format, args), where the arguments are taken from the statistics info.
note: macro defined at zfcp_sysfs.c:750-764 and instantiated at 766 onward; the old prose (adapter must support measurement) matches this macro rather than ZFCP_DEFINE_A_ATTR.

name: zfcp_unit_remove
prose: Precondition: port is a zfcp_port; fcp_lun is the LUN to remove. Postcondition: under port->unit_list_lock (write, irq-disabling) it calls _zfcp_unit_find and, if a unit is found, removes it from the port's unit list; after unlocking it returns -EINVAL if no unit was found. Otherwise it looks up the unit's scsi_device and, if one exists, calls scsi_remove_device and scsi_device_put, then calls device_unregister on the unit's device, drops the reference taken by _zfcp_unit_find with put_device, and returns 0.
note: listed as an unnamed teardown function with prose 'always returns 0' and a caller-held reference; the function is zfcp_unit_remove (zfcp_unit.c:238-263) which returns -EINVAL when no unit exists and does its own _zfcp_unit_find.

name: process_selection
prose: Precondition: host is a valid Scsi_Host with an NCR_700_Host_Parameters, dsp is the script address at which the chip was interrupted. Postcondition: it reads the selected/reselecting ID register (CTEST9 on the 710, SFBR otherwise) up to 5 times, masking out the host's own ID bit and stopping at the first non-zero value (5 microsecond delay between reads), then reads SBCL: if the IO bit is clear it sets id to 0xff (the chip was selected, not reselected); otherwise it stores bitmap_to_number(id) in hostdata->reselection_id. If hostdata->state is NCR_700_HOST_BUSY and hostdata->cmd is non-NULL, it handles the interrupted command according to dsp: at the Disconnect1/2, 3/4, 5/6 or 7/8 entries it calls save_for_reselection with the matching resume point, at Finish1/2 it calls process_script_interrupt with A_GOOD_STATUS_AFTER_STATUS, and for any other dsp it sets the command's slot state to NCR_700_SLOT_QUEUED. Whatever happened, it then sets hostdata->state to NCR_700_HOST_BUSY, hostdata->cmd to NULL, clears msgin[1] and syncs msgin to the device. It returns the script address pScript + Ent_SelectedAsTarget if id is 0xff, pScript + Ent_GetReselectionWithTag if the reselecting ID has its tag_negotiated bit set, and pScript + Ent_GetReselectionData otherwise.
note: 'unnamed reselection handler fragment' is process_selection (53c700.c:1292-1369); slice cut the head. Previously dropped.

name: bitmap_to_number
prose: Precondition: bitmap is a __u8. Postcondition: returns the index (0 to 7) of the lowest set bit of bitmap, or 8 if bitmap is 0. It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= bitmap && bitmap <= 255; ensures 0 <= result && result <= 8 && (result == 8 ==> bitmap == 0) && (result < 8 ==> (bitmap & (1 << result)) != 0) && (\forall integer j; 0 <= j < result ==> (bitmap & (1 << j)) == 0); */
note: 'unnamed_ffs_helper' is bitmap_to_number (53c700.c:511-519). The earlier contract failed to parse (forall written without backslash); this one follows the code: loop over i < 8 while the bit is clear.

name: blogic_rdconfig
prose: Precondition: adapter points to a blogic_adapter whose I/O and command interface can be used (and, for FlashPoint types, whose fpinfo has been filled by the probe). Postcondition: returns true after filling the adapter's configuration fields, and false (through blogic_failure, which logs the step) when an adapter command fails or the firmware is too old. For a FlashPoint type it fills model ('BT-' plus the fpinfo model), fw_ver (FLASHPOINT_FW_VER), SCSI id, translation, parity, reset, wide, termination, SCAM, sync/fast/ultra/wide/disconnect permissions, queue depth 255 and CCB counts from fpinfo and constants and jumps to the common tail. For other types it issues the commands INQUIRE BOARD ID, CONFIGURATION, SETUP INFORMATION, EXTENDED SETUP INFORMATION and, when the firmware major digit is above '0', the firmware 3rd digit, determines the model number (from fixed cases or INQUIRE HOST ADAPTER MODEL NUMBER), builds model and firmware version strings (adding the firmware letter via a further command when the version is at least 3.3), and stores SCSI id, bus type, IRQ (from config only if irq_ch is 0), extended translation, scatter-gather limits, level-int, wide, differential, SCAM, ultra, extended-LUN, termination (W series, via INQUIRE PCI HOST ADAPTER INFORMATION), AutoSCSI permissions (firmware 4.x and 5.x, via FETCH HOST ADAPTER LOCAL RAM), S/A-series defaults (firmware below 4), max devices and LUNs, queue depths, mailbox count, strict round robin, CCB counts, tagged-queuing permissions and BIOS address; it returns false with 'Too old firmware' for a BT-445S with the BIOS enabled and firmware below 3.37. The common tail builds full_model, per-target queue depths (from driver options when given), untagged queue depth, tagged-queue permission masks, bus settle time, and then returns true.
note: listed name blogic_probe1 does not exist; the slice 1363-1663 lies inside blogic_rdconfig (BusLogic.c:1234-1687), which matches the 'fields populated or blogic_failure' prose. Read in full; the prose summarises the field assignments rather than listing every field.

name: FPT_ssel
prose: Precondition: p_card indexes valid FPT_BL_Card and FPT_sccbMgrTbl entries, the card's currentSCCB is a valid initialised SCCB whose TargID selects the target's entry, port is that card's I/O base. Postcondition: it switches the card to ARAM access at entry (ARAM_ACCESS) and back to SGRAM access (SGRAM_ACCESS) before every return. It clears F_USE_CMD_Q if the target's tag status is TAG_Q_REJECT and selects the LUN (the SCCB's Lun when F_CONLUN_IO is set and the target is not TAG_Q_TRYING, else 0). It then returns early, after calling FPT_queueSelectFail, in these cases: tagging has started (F_TAG_STARTED), the command does not use command queueing, the target has TarLUN_CA == 0 and is TAG_Q_TRYING and TarTagQ_Cnt is non-zero (TarLUNBusy[lun] set to 1 first); tagging started, the command uses command queueing and TarLUN_CA == 1 (TarLUNBusy is not set); discQCount is at least QUEUE_DEPTH, or no free discQ_Tbl slot is found in the first scan, when the command is non-tagged or F_CONLUN_IO applies (TarLUNBusy set to 1 first); and no free slot is found in the tag-assignment scan for a command-queued command (TarLUNBusy set to 1 first). Otherwise it marks TarLUNBusy[lun], may reserve a discQ_Tbl slot, writes the target id, and loads the select automation by case: RESET_COMMAND loads the target-reset message, sets Sccb_scsistat to SELECT_BDR_ST, resets the target's sync/wide status per EEPROM flags and reinitialises the target table; Sccb_scsistat == ABORT_ST loads the abort message sequence; otherwise if wide is not negotiated it calls FPT_siwidn (SELECT_WN_ST) or, if sync is not supported, FPT_sisyncn (SELECT_SN_ST). If no automation was loaded it loads a tagged select (SELECT_Q_ST, with a tag taken from discQ_Tbl and stored in Sccb_tag and tagQ_Lst) or a non-tagged select (SELECT_ST; also used when the target rejects tags) and downloads the CDB. Finally it clears FIFO/status registers, and either starts a target select with ENA_ATN/ENA_RESEL (when F_DEV_SELECTED is not set) or writes AUTO_IMMED to autostart_3 with DISABLE_AUTO, and returns.
note: 'unnamed target selection routine' is FPT_ssel (FlashPoint.c:2275-2564), read in full. The old prose said the function was entered with ARAM access on and that TarLUNBusy was set on every early return; the function switches to ARAM itself and the TarLUN_CA == 1 early return does not set TarLUNBusy.

name: FPT_autoCmdCmplt
prose: Precondition: p_card indexes valid FPT_BL_Card and FPT_sccbMgrTbl entries, the card's currentSCCB points to a valid SCCB, p_port is that card's I/O base. Postcondition: it reads the status byte from p_port + hp_gp_reg_0 and clears the target's TarLUN_CA. If the status is SAM_STAT_TASK_SET_FULL it marks the LUN busy (TarLUNBusy[currSCCB->Lun] when F_CONLUN_IO is set and the target is not TAG_Q_TRYING, else TarLUNBusy[0]), decrements discQCount if non-zero, clears the matching discQ_Tbl entry (by LunDiscQ_Idx[Lun], by Sccb_tag, or by LunDiscQ_Idx[0]), sets F_STATUSLOADED, calls FPT_queueSelectFail and returns without setting SCCB_ERROR. If the status is not GOOD and the SCCB is in SELECT_SN_ST (or SELECT_WN_ST) it updates the target's sync (or wide) negotiation bits in TarStatus and TarEEValue, sets F_NEW_SCCB_CMD, marks the LUN busy and clears the discQ entry as above, and returns without setting SCCB_ERROR. For another non-GOOD status: if it is CHECK_CONDITION and F_DO_RENEGO is set it clears the target's sync mask bits (if EE_SYNC_MASK is set in TarEEValue) and wide mask bits (if EE_WIDE_SCSI is set); then, if the SCCB is not in auto-sense state it sets SCCB_ERROR and TargetStatus to the status byte, and for CHECK_CONDITION it sets TarLUN_CA to 1 and, when RequestSenseLength is not NO_AUTO_REQUEST_SENSE, raises RequestSenseLength to 14 if it was 0, calls FPT_ssenss, sets F_NEW_SCCB_CMD, marks the LUN busy, clears the discQ entry and returns. In every other case (GOOD status, a non-GOOD status in auto-sense state, a non-GOOD status other than CHECK_CONDITION, or CHECK_CONDITION with NO_AUTO_REQUEST_SENSE) it clears TarLUNBusy (indexed by Lun or 0 as above) and calls FPT_queueCmdComplete.
note: reviewer (round 15: the remaining cases do not clear TarLUNBusy or call FPT_queueCmdComplete) wrong: FlashPoint.c:4855-4863 does both. Round 2 (TarLUN_CA set for any CHECK_CONDITION, not only when sense is auto-requested) is already how the text reads (line 4781-4784). Function at FlashPoint.c:4614-4864.

name: NCR5380_select
prose: Precondition: the caller holds hostdata->lock with interrupts disabled (the function drops and retakes it; it is declared __releases/__acquires), cmd is the command to select. Postcondition: it sets hostdata->selecting = cmd, starts arbitration and waits (lock dropped) up to one second; the lock is held again whenever it returns, and hostdata->selecting is NULL on every return. Result is false in these cases: the mid layer cleared hostdata->selecting while the lock was dropped (checked after arbitration, after the settle delay, in the 250 ms response case and after the REQ wait, in the last case do_abort is called); the target did not respond within 250 ms while selecting was still set (cmd->result = DID_BAD_TARGET << 16 and complete_cmd called); the IDENTIFY message transfer left bytes untransferred (cmd->result = DID_ERROR << 16 and complete_cmd called); or the nexus was established (hostdata->connected = cmd, the LUN bit set in hostdata->busy[], initialize_SCp called). Result is true (the attempt was abandoned without completing cmd, selecting still being set at the exit label) when a reselection interrupt cleared MR_ARBITRATE, arbitration timed out or was lost, a reselection was found after arbitration was won (NCR5380_reselect is called), or the target did not assert REQ within one second.
note: reviewer (round 15: the function acquires hostdata->lock itself so the caller must not hold it) wrong: it unlocks first (NCR5380.c:1007 spin_unlock_irq) and reacquires, as __releases/__acquires says. The common exit at 1222-1226 returns false when selecting was already NULL. Function at 963-1227.

name: aac_scsi_cmd
prose: Precondition: scsicmd is a scsi_cmnd for a device of this adapter. Postcondition: returns -1 without completing the command if dev->fsa_dev is NULL. For a target other than the controller itself on the container channel: an id out of range or non-zero LUN completes the command with DID_NO_CONNECT and returns 0; if the container is not valid or reports NOT_READY, SERVICE_ACTION_IN_16 (only READ CAPACITY(16) on a raw 64-bit interface), INQUIRY, READ_CAPACITY and TEST_UNIT_READY return -1 when dev->in_reset is set and otherwise return the result of _aac_probe_container. On other channels it returns aac_send_hba_fib (native raw device) or aac_send_srb_fib (non-dasd, physicals exposed or jbod), each returning -1 first when dev->in_reset is set, else completes with DID_NO_CONNECT and returns 0. For the controller itself, commands other than INQUIRY and TEST_UNIT_READY complete with CHECK CONDITION (illegal request sense) and return 0. Remaining dispatch on cmnd[0]: READ and WRITE variants return -1 when in_reset is set, else aac_read or aac_write; SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE completes GOOD when (aac_cache & 6) == 6 and the cache is protected, returns aac_synchronize when (aac_cache & 6) != 2, else falls into INQUIRY handling; INQUIRY with the EVPD bit and aac_wwn builds the supported-pages, serial-number (0x80) or device-id (0x83) pages (for 0x80 and 0x83 returns aac_get_container_serial when aac_wwn != 2) or an unsupported-page CHECK CONDITION, a standard INQUIRY for the controller itself completes GOOD, and for any other target returns -1 when in_reset is set, else returns aac_get_container_name; SERVICE_ACTION_IN_16 (READ CAPACITY(16), raw 64-bit interface), READ_CAPACITY, MODE_SENSE, MODE_SENSE_10, REQUEST_SENSE, ALLOW_MEDIUM_REMOVAL, TEST_UNIT_READY (CHECK CONDITION when NOT_READY) and the no-op commands fill the reply and complete GOOD; START_STOP returns aac_start_stop; unknown commands complete with CHECK CONDITION. Paths that complete the command call aac_scsi_done and return 0.
note: reviewer (round 15: -1 on in_reset is not universal and the INQUIRY/container_name path depends on the target) mixed: the old text was right that container INQUIRY returns aac_get_container_name (aachba.c:2963) but in_reset gives -1 only on specific paths (2813, 2827, 2832, 2863, 2871, 2958), not for READ CAPACITY or MODE SENSE. Name was not visible in the slice; function at aachba.c:2773-3255, read in full.

name: aac_build_sgraw2
prose: Precondition: scsicmd has a DMA-mappable buffer, rio2 points to a valid aac_raw_io2 whose sge array holds at least sg_max entries, and sg_max is at least the number of mapped segments (BUG_ON otherwise). Postcondition: it calls scsi_dma_map; if that returns 0 or a negative value it returns it and rio2 is untouched. Otherwise it fills rio2->sge[0..nseg-1] from the segments, sets sgeFirstSize from the first segment and, when nseg >= 2, sgeNominalSize from the second, decides whether the list is conformable, trims the last entry and the byte count to scsi_bufflen if the mapped total is larger, sets sgeCnt to nseg and RIO2_SG_FORMAT_IEEE1212. If the list is not conformable and a page-size factor i >= 1 exists with the converted count nseg_new <= sg_max, it calls aac_convert_sgraw2: that returns 0 without changing anything when the aac_convert_sgl parameter is 0 (so RIO2_SGL_CONFORMANT stays unset), returns -ENOMEM if its allocation fails (and this function returns that -ENOMEM with sgeCnt and the format flag already set, the mapped segments still mapped), and otherwise rewrites the middle entries and sets sgeCnt, sgeNominalSize and RIO2_SGL_CONFORMANT. If the list is conformable it sets RIO2_SGL_CONFORMANT. A byte count below scsicmd->underflow only logs a warning. It returns the byte count.
note: reviewer (round 15: RIO2_SGL_CONFORMANT is not set when aac_convert_sgraw2 is disabled) right, aachba.c:4010-4011. Function at aachba.c:3923-4002.

name: aac_send_raw_srb
prose: Precondition: dev is a live aacraid adapter, arg is a user pointer to a struct user_aac_srb followed by room for the reply. Postcondition: returns -EBUSY if dev->in_reset is set, -EPERM if the caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN, -ENOMEM if aac_fib_alloc fails. After the fib is allocated, errors go to a cleanup label with: -EFAULT when the SRB size cannot be copied from user space; -EINVAL when the size is out of range, the scatter-gather count exceeds the embedded limit, an sg list is present with no data direction, the size does not match the sg count, or an sg entry exceeds the limit; PTR_ERR from memdup_user; -ENOMEM from an sg buffer allocation; -EFAULT when outbound sg data or inbound data or the reply cannot be copied; -ERESTARTSYS if the send returns -ERESTARTSYS; and -ENXIO if the send returns any other non-zero value. It builds either a native HBA command (when the target is a native raw device, sent with aac_hba_send) or an SRB (sent with aac_fib_send, 32 or 64 bit sg format depending on the adapter). On success it copies inbound data and the reply to user space and returns 0. At cleanup it always frees the copy of the user SRB; unless the result is -ERESTARTSYS it also frees the sg buffers and completes and frees the fib, and for -ERESTARTSYS it leaves the fib and sg buffers allocated.
note: listed name aac_ioctl_send_raw_srb does not exist; the function is aac_send_raw_srb (commctrl.c:479-996). The earlier text said every error releases the fib and sg buffers and that the send status is returned; neither holds (-ERESTARTSYS skips the release, other send errors become -ENXIO). Read in full.

name: aac_handle_aif
prose: Precondition: fibptr is a fib whose hw_fib_va holds an AIF command; dev may be NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing; it returns at once if dev or dev->fsa_dev is NULL. Otherwise it dispatches on the AIF command. AifCmdDriverNotify: for AifRawDeviceRemove (valid channel and id) it queues a DELETE of the physical device, for AifDenMorphComplete and AifDenVolumeExtendComplete with an in-range container and a found scsi_device it sets config_needed to CHANGE and config_waiting_on to AifEnConfigChange for that container; AifCmdEventNotify: AifEnBatteryEvent sets dev->cache_protected to true when data word 1 equals 3 and to false otherwise (this is the only place cache_protected is written); AifEnAddContainer, AifEnDeleteContainer and AifEnContainerChange (the last only when not already waiting within AIF_SNIFF_TIMEOUT) set config_needed ADD, DELETE or CHANGE and config_waiting_on AifEnConfigChange with a timestamp for an in-range container; AifEnAddJBOD and AifEnDeleteJBOD queue an ADD or DELETE of a physical device (for ADD an existing scsi_device is removed first); AifEnEnclosureManagement (when not in JBOD mode) queues an ADD or DELETE for drive insertion/removal events; AifBuManagerEvent calls aac_handle_aif_bu; AifCmdJobProgress sets config_waiting_on, config_needed (ADD or DELETE) and the stamp for all containers only when the job-control fields show a completed or running clear. For the first two commands, after command-specific handling, it clears config_waiting_on for the one container or for all containers when the waiting event equals data word 0 and the stamp is within AIF_SNIFF_TIMEOUT. Finally, starting at container 0, if no action is pending it looks for a container with no wait, a non-NOTHING config_needed and a fresh stamp and takes that action; if nothing is pending, or dev->scsi_host_ptr is NULL, it returns. Otherwise for the container channel it sets valid from 1 to 2 and calls aac_probe_container, looks up the scsi_device at channel, id, lun and, if found, offlines it (DELETE), or onlines it if offline and then rescans it or offlines it when the container is no longer valid (ADD and CHANGE), puts the reference; if no device was found and the action is ADD it calls scsi_add_device. For the container channel it then moves to the next container and repeats the scan until the containers are exhausted.
note: reviewer (round 15: only one container is probed, the scan does not repeat) wrong: commsup.c:1453-1457 increments container and jumps back to retry_next. Round 2 (non-NULL invalid dev dereferenced) concerns the caller contract, not the code. Function at commsup.c:1054-1458, read in full.

name: aac_fib_send
prose: Precondition: fibptr is a struct fib whose dev and hw_fib_va are valid, size is the payload length after the fib header, the caller holds none of dev->manage_lock, dev->sync_lock or fibptr->event_lock and may sleep. Postcondition: returns -EBUSY if the header's XferState lacks HostOwned and -EINVAL if it has AdapterProcessed (both with nothing modified); then it clears fibptr->flags and returns -EINVAL if wait is non-zero and reply is zero; sets the Async/ResponseExpected or NoResponseExpected XferState bits from wait and reply, SenderFibAddress, Handle, Command, SentFromHost and Size, and returns -EMSGSIZE if the size exceeds SenderSize; sets NormalPriority, stores callback, callback_data and FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG when wait is zero and clears fibptr->done; returns -EBUSY if dev->queues is NULL. For a waiting call it takes a management slot (returning -EBUSY without changing the count when dev->management_fib_count >= AAC_NUM_MGT_FIB) and the count stays incremented on every later path except a failed aac_adapter_deliver, which returns -EBUSY after decrementing it. In sync mode it queues the fib on sync_fib_list or makes it dev->sync_fib and issues aac_adapter_sync_cmd, then returns 0 when waiting and not interrupted, -EFAULT when the wait was interrupted, and -EINPROGRESS when not waiting. Otherwise, after successful delivery it returns -EINPROGRESS (reply set) or 0 (reply clear) when wait is zero; for a waiting call with wait < 0 it polls up to 3 minutes and returns -ETIMEDOUT on timeout, or -EFAULT if the PCI device is offline or aac_adapter_check_health reports a blinkLED; with wait > 0 it waits interruptibly; afterwards it returns -ERESTARTSYS (setting fibptr->done to 2) if done is still 0, -ETIMEDOUT if FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG_TIMED_OUT is set, and 0 otherwise. No spin lock is held on return.
note: commsup.c:475-697. Previously unreviewed; re-read and checked against the source, wording tightened (the -EBUSY for a full management table leaves the count unchanged; the -EMSGSIZE and queue checks come after header fields are written).

name: aac_hba_send
prose: Precondition: fibptr is a struct fib whose dev and hw_fib_va are valid (hw_fib_va holds a native HBA command request), callback is NULL or a valid fib_callback, the caller holds neither dev->manage_lock nor fibptr->event_lock and may sleep. Postcondition: it sets fibptr->flags to FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG | FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG_NATIVE_HBA, stores callback and callback_data when callback is non-NULL (no waiting then) and writes hbacmd->iu_type = command; it returns -EINVAL when command is not HBA_IU_TYPE_SCSI_CMD_REQ (before request_id and the management count are touched). Otherwise it sets request_id and FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG_SCSI_CMD. A synchronous call (callback NULL) takes a management slot, returning -EBUSY with no change if dev->management_fib_count >= AAC_NUM_MGT_FIB; if aac_adapter_deliver fails it returns -EBUSY and, for a synchronous call, undoes the count increment, which otherwise stays on later paths. After delivery with a callback it returns -EINPROGRESS. For a synchronous call it returns -EFAULT if aac_pci_offline is true, otherwise waits interruptibly (setting done to 2 if interrupted), returns -ERESTARTSYS when done is 0 or 2 afterwards (writing done = 2), -ETIMEDOUT if FIB_CONTEXT_FLAG_TIMED_OUT is set, and 0 otherwise. No spin lock is held on return.
note: commsup.c:699-779. Previously unreviewed; re-read and checked against the source.

name: AdvInitAsc3550Driver
prose: Precondition: asc_dvc points to an ADV_DVC_VAR whose iop_base, drv_ptr->dev, cfg, bios_ctrl, wdtr_able, sdtr_able, ultra_able and chip_scsi_id are valid. Postcondition: returns ADV_ERROR (leaving err_code unchanged) if err_code is already non-zero, and returns ADV_ERROR with err_code ASC_IERR_BAD_CHIPTYPE if chip_type is not ADV_CHIP_ASC3550. It saves the BIOS RAM region and per-target values, then calls request_firmware: on failure it sets err_code to ASC_IERR_MCODE_CHKSUM and returns the negative errno; if the image is shorter than 4 bytes it releases the firmware, sets that err_code and returns -EINVAL. It loads the microcode with AdvLoadMicrocode, stores its result in err_code and releases the firmware (on every path after request_firmware succeeded); a non-zero result returns ADV_ERROR. It then restores the BIOS region, writes the code checksum, version, chip type and operating variables, and returns ADV_ERROR with err_code OR-ed with ASC_IERR_ILLEGAL_CONNECTION (illegal connector use), ASC_IERR_REVERSED_CABLE or ASC_IERR_SINGLE_END_DEVICE when those checks fail; it also returns ADV_ERROR with err_code OR-ed with ASC_IERR_NO_CARRIER if the ICQ or IRQ carrier cannot be obtained. After starting the RISC it either restores saved values (BIOS signature present) or resets the SCSI bus when BIOS_CTRL_RESET_SCSI_BUS is set, and returns 0, or ASC_WARN_BUSRESET_ERROR if the bus reset failed.
note: listed name AdvInitAsc3550Dev does not exist; the function is AdvInitAsc3550Driver (advansys.c:4350-4781), read in full. The earlier prose omitted the already-set-error, bad-chip-type, no-carrier and warning returns.

name: AdvInitAsc38C1600Driver
prose: Precondition: asc_dvc points to an initialised ADV_DVC_VAR for an ASC38C1600 whose EEPROM-derived configuration and chip are accessible. Postcondition: returns ADV_ERROR if err_code is already non-zero, and ADV_ERROR with err_code ASC_IERR_BAD_CHIPTYPE if chip_type is not ADV_CHIP_ASC38C1600. It runs the RAM built-in self test: a failed pre-test returns ADV_ERROR with err_code ASC_IERR_BIST_PRE_TEST, and a failed RAM test stores the status in bist_err_code and returns ADV_ERROR with ASC_IERR_BIST_RAM_TEST. It then calls request_firmware, returning the negative errno with err_code ASC_IERR_MCODE_CHKSUM on failure and -EINVAL (same err_code) for an image shorter than 4 bytes, loads the microcode with AdvLoadMicrocode, releases the firmware and returns ADV_ERROR if the load failed. After programming the microcode defaults it returns ADV_ERROR with err_code OR-ed with ASC_IERR_REVERSED_CABLE, ASC_IERR_HVD_DEVICE or ASC_IERR_NO_CARRIER (no carrier for the ICQ or IRQ) when those conditions are found, and otherwise returns 0, or ASC_WARN_BUSRESET_ERROR if a required SCSI bus reset failed.
note: listed name AdvInitAsc38C1600 does not exist; function is AdvInitAsc38C1600Driver (advansys.c:5279-). Only part was read line by line: I read the head and tail and checked every return/err_code assignment with a grep over lines 5279-5790; the middle (register and LRAM programming) was not read.

name: AscIsrChipHalted
prose: Precondition: asc_dvc is non-NULL with a non-NULL drv_ptr (BUG_ON otherwise); the adapter's halt-code word, current-CDB byte and the halted queue entry are readable. Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads the halt code and the halted queue; for a recognised halt code it clears the halt-code word to 0 before returning, and for an unrecognised code it returns without doing anything (the halt code stays). ASC_HALT_DISABLE_ASYN_USE_SYN_FIX and ASC_HALT_ENABLE_ASYN_USE_SYN_FIX write the chip SDTR value and boardp->sdtr_data[tid] (0 or the async value) only when the target's pci_fix_asyn_xfer bit is set. ASC_HALT_EXTMSG_IN reads the extended message: for a valid SDTR it limits the offset and period, may mark the SDTR not accepted, and then: if the offset is 0 it clears QC_MSG_OUT and the init_sdtr and sdtr_done bits and sets the chip SDTR to the async value (without updating boardp->sdtr_data or pci_fix_asyn_xfer); otherwise it either accepts the request (clearing QC_MSG_OUT, setting sdtr_done and init_sdtr, clearing the pci_fix bit, programming the chip SDTR and boardp->sdtr_data) or sends a counter-proposal with AscMsgOutSDTR (setting QC_MSG_OUT) and programs the same values; the queue control byte is written back; a WDTR is answered with width 0 and a MESSAGE_REJECT is sent for any other extended message, both setting QC_MSG_OUT. ASC_HALT_CHK_CONDITION sets QC_REQ_SENSE, re-sends an SDTR and clears the sdtr_done bit when init_sdtr has the target bit, rewrites the tag code and the queue status and clears the target's SCSIBUSY bit. ASC_HALT_SDTR_REJECTED clears init_sdtr and sdtr_done and restores the async SDTR when the rejected message was an SDTR, and clears QC_MSG_OUT. ASC_HALT_SS_QUEUE_FULL sets the target's SCSIBUSY and queue_full_or_busy bits when the chip and driver queue counts are non-zero and, for TASK_SET_FULL with a count above ASC_MIN_TAGGED_CMD, decrements it and stores it in max_dvc_qng, the LRAM byte, boardp->queue_full and queue_full_cnt.
note: reviewer (round 15: a valid SDTR with req_ack_offset 0 does not update boardp->sdtr_data or pci_fix_asyn_xfer) right, advansys.c:6388-6393. Function at advansys.c:6294-6591, read in full.

name: makecode
prose: Precondition: hosterr and scsierr are adapter status codes, each at most 0xff for the contract. Postcondition: returns scsierr OR-ed with the translated host status shifted left by 16, where hosterr 0x0, 0xa and 0xb translate to 0, 0x11 to DID_TIME_OUT (3), 0x14 to DID_RESET (8), 0x12, 0x13, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19 and 0x1a to DID_ERROR (7), and any other hosterr value is passed through unchanged after a printk error message. It writes no state besides the log message.
contract: /*@ requires hosterr <= 0xff && scsierr <= 0xff; ensures result == (scsierr | ((((hosterr == 0x0 || hosterr == 0xa || hosterr == 0xb) ? 0 : (hosterr == 0x11) ? 3 : (hosterr == 0x14) ? 8 : (hosterr == 0x12 || hosterr == 0x13 || hosterr == 0x15 || hosterr == 0x16 || hosterr == 0x17 || hosterr == 0x18 || hosterr == 0x19 || hosterr == 0x1a) ? 7 : hosterr) << 16))); */
note: aha1542.c:140-205. Reviewer (rounds 2 and 15: the formal contract omits the printk for an unknown hosterr) is about a log message, not state, so the contract is kept, while the prose now mentions the log; DID_* values 3, 7, 8 confirmed in scsi_status.h:48-53, so round 1 (numeric values wrong) no longer applies.

name: aha1542_hw_init
prose: Precondition: tpnt is the host template, pdev the parent device, indx indexes the io[] module parameter arrays. Postcondition: returns NULL if io[indx] is 0 or request_region for the adapter's AHA1542_REGION_SIZE ports fails (nothing acquired). Otherwise it allocates a Scsi_Host (NULL result releases the region and returns NULL), tests the port, sets bus times, queries and reads the configuration; a failure of any of these, of dma_set_mask_and_coherent, or of the mailbox allocation puts the host and releases the region and returns NULL. A CCB allocation failure frees the mailbox buffer first; a failure of request_irq frees the CCB and mailbox buffers; a failure of request_dma (when a DMA channel is configured) frees the irq as well; a scsi_add_host failure also frees the DMA channel if one was requested; in each case the host is put, the region released and NULL returned. On success it registers and scans the host and returns the Scsi_Host, leaving the I/O region, mailbox and CCB buffers, IRQ and DMA channel held.
note: listed name aha1542_probe does not exist; the slice holds aha1542_hw_init (aha1542.c:740-838), which returns a Scsi_Host pointer and releases in the reverse order described. The old prose called pdev a PCI device and said the host was already allocated; neither is so.

name: ahd_handle_seqint
prose: Precondition: ahd is an initialised aic79xx softc whose sequencer is paused and has raised a sequencer interrupt; intstat holds the interrupt status. Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads SEQINTCODE and clears the SEQINT bit (it does not return early if SEQINT was not set), applies the INTCOLLISION workaround when that bug flag is set (unpausing, waiting until the sequencer pauses again and clearing SEQINT again), updates the mode state, and handles the code with a switch: ENTERING_NONPACK, INVALID_SEQINT, STATUS_OVERRUN (which panics 'For safety'), ILLEGAL_PHASE, DUMP_CARD_STATE, PDATA_REINIT, HOST_MSG_LOOP, NO_MATCH, PROTO_VIOLATION, IGN_WIDE_RES, BAD_PHASE, MISSED_BUSFREE, DATA_OVERRUN, MKMSG_FAILED, TASKMGMT_FUNC_COMPLETE (which panics on an unexpected task-management function), TASKMGMT_CMD_CMPLT_OKAY, TRACEPOINT0-3 (logged), NO_SEQINT (nothing), SAW_HWERR (ahd_handle_hwerrint) and a default that logs an unexpected code. HOST_MSG_LOOP with a bus phase other than MESGIN or MESGOUT dumps the card state, clears the interrupt status, calls ahd_restart and returns without unpausing; MISSED_BUSFREE logs, calls ahd_restart and returns without unpausing. Every other path leaves the switch and ends with ahd_unpause.
note: reviewer (round 15: early returns exist for SEQINT not set or an invalid INTCOLLISION code) wrong: there is no such check; the early returns are the two ahd_restart cases (aic79xx_core.c:2074-2075, 2181-2182). Real name ahd_handle_seqint (1769-2370). Partly read: the head (1769-1830), the tail and the list of case labels, returns and panics were read; the case bodies were not read line by line.

name: ahd_setup_initiator_msgout
prose: Precondition: ahd is a valid softc, scb is NULL or a valid SCB with a valid hscb, devinfo is valid whenever scb is non-NULL (the final panic path reads devinfo->target_mask, and the negotiation path uses it), ahd->msgout_buf has room for the bytes queued. Postcondition: msgout_index and msgout_len are first set to 0 and MSG_FLAG_PACKETIZED is set if ahd_currently_packetized(ahd). If send_msg_perror is non-zero and the MSG_OUT register equals HOST_MSG it stores that one byte (msgout_index and msgout_len become 1), sets msg_type to MSG_TYPE_INITIATOR_MSGOUT and returns without clearing MK_MESSAGE or SCSISEQ0. Otherwise, if scb is NULL it prints a warning, stores NOP (msgout_index and msgout_len become 1), sets msg_type and returns the same way. Otherwise, if the SCB is neither SCB_DEVICE_RESET nor SCB_PACKETIZED and MSG_OUT equals MSG_IDENTIFYFLAG it appends an identify byte (with the LUN, and the disconnect flag when DISCENB is set) and, when TAG_ENB is set, the tag-type byte and tag. Then, independently of that: SCB_DEVICE_RESET appends TARGET_RESET and clears SCSISEQ0; else SCB_ABORT appends ABORT_TASK (with TAG_ENB) or ABORT_TASK_SET and clears SCSISEQ0; else SCB_AUTO_NEGOTIATE or SCB_NEGOTIATE calls ahd_build_transfer_msg and clears SCSISEQ0; else it prints diagnostics and panics, even if identify bytes were queued. On the paths that reach the end it clears MK_MESSAGE in the hardware SCB_CONTROL and in hscb->control, sets msgout_index to 0 and msg_type to MSG_TYPE_INITIATOR_MSGOUT; msgout_len is the number of bytes queued.
note: reviewer (round 15: the precondition omits devinfo validity for the panic path that reads devinfo->target_mask) right, aic79xx_core.c:4462-4463. Function at 4365-4479.

name: ahd_handle_message_phase
prose: Precondition: ahd is a valid softc whose sequencer raised a REQINIT during a message phase and ahd->msg_type is one of MSG_TYPE_INITIATOR_MSGOUT, MSG_TYPE_INITIATOR_MSGIN, MSG_TYPE_TARGET_MSGIN or MSG_TYPE_TARGET_MSGOUT. Postcondition: returns nothing. It fetches the device info and the last bus phase, retries a LQIPHASE_OUTPKT condition with LQIRETRY, and services one byte according to msg_type, writing SCSIBUS/SCSIDAT-related registers, RETURN_1/RETURN_2 and updating msgin_index/msgout_index; it may switch msg_type (INITIATOR_MSGOUT to INITIATOR_MSGIN when a message-in phase is seen, INITIATOR_MSGIN back to INITIATOR_MSGOUT when a message-out phase is seen and a message is waiting, TARGET_MSGOUT to TARGET_MSGIN when a response is pending), asserts ATN when a parsed message has a response and drops ATN on the last outgoing byte. When the session ends (end_session) it calls ahd_clear_msg_state and then either (packetized messages) logs, sets LASTPHASE, SEQ_FLAGS and resets the sequencer to the idle loop, or writes EXIT_MSG_LOOP to RETURN_1. It returns immediately without that cleanup when ahd_parse_msg returns MSGLOOP_TERMINATED in the MSG_TYPE_TARGET_MSGOUT case (in the INITIATOR_MSGIN case MSGLOOP_TERMINATED ends the session with cleanup). It panics (does not return) in three cases: MSG_TYPE_INITIATOR_MSGOUT with msgout_len == 0 and send_msg_perror == 0, MSG_TYPE_TARGET_MSGIN with msgout_len == 0, and an unknown msg_type. No locks or references are taken or released.
note: listed name ahd_handle_reqinit does not exist; the slice is ahd_handle_message_phase (aic79xx_core.c:4677-5008), read in full. The earlier prose listed only two of the three panics.
